display.title: Episode 28: The Mountain of Ice
display.summary_short: Rabbi Meir of Premishlan walks down icy steps every winter morning without slipping; two mocking visitors try it and tumble down, then learn his secret: be tied to Hashem above.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi thanks listeners and the schools, near and far, that have asked for tapes of the program, and leads the Hakochainik march. The story is 'The Mountain of Ice'. In Premishlan, a mikvah stood atop a steep mountain; in winter everyone took the long winding road, but Rabbi Meir of Premishlan walked calmly up and down the icy steps every morning. Before the story continues, a nine-year-old yeshiva student recites the Shema in Studio 604. Two travelers stranded in Premishlan by snow, who had never seen a Rebbe, laugh at the townspeople's awe and try the steps themselves. They slip and roll to the bottom, and the townspeople kindly nurse them back to health. Ashamed, they ask the Rebbe's forgiveness and his secret. He answers in Yiddish: whoever is tied to Hashem above does not fall down below. Uncle Yossi explains that we tie ourselves to Hashem through Torah and mitzvos. After a sponsor message and a Dial-a-Jewish-Story announcement, he speaks of bringing true peace through Torah, prayer and tzedakah, and the coming of Moshiach.
display.lesson: When we tie ourselves to Hashem through Torah and mitzvos, we will not fall, even on the most slippery path.
